'''Susan Schechter Bortner''' (published as '''Susan Schechter''') is an American [[Survey methodology|survey statistician]], formerly in US Government service and now a researcher at [[NORC at the University of Chicago]], a private nonprofit social research organization.

==Education and career==
Schechter graduated from [[Montgomery Blair High School]] in [[Maryland]] in 1972.{{r|mbhs}} She earned a bachelor's degree in [[criminology]] from the [[University of Maryland, College Park]], and a master's degree in human development from [[Antioch University]].{{r|norc|bradburn}}

Her positions in government service included working as a survey researcher in the [[National Center for Health Statistics]], as a senior statistician in the [[Office of Management and Budget]], focusing on the classification of race and ethnicity, and in the [[United States Census Bureau]], where she headed the [[American Community Survey]] from 2006 to 2010. After more than 25 years of government work, she moved to [[NORC at the University of Chicago]] in 2010, where she became Project Director for the Medicare Current Beneficiary Survey.{{r|norc|bradburn}}

==Recognition==
Schechter was named a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 2005.{{r|fellow}} She chaired the Social Statistics Section of the American Statistical Association in 2006.{{r|chair}} In 2017, NORC gave her their Norman Bradburn Career Achievement Award.{{r|bradburn}}
